correctness.rationale: For C(n,4), n>=5, Gale evenness identifies the tetrahedral facets exactly as unions of disjoint edges of a cyclic n-gon. Every facet produces precisely three double-graph edges, hence V=n(n-1)/2 and E=3n(n-3)/2. Arc-shortening moves connect all vertices for odd n, and exactly the index-difference parity classes for even n; the even component vertex/edge counts produce the asserted circle-wedge ranks. The graph chain exact sequence gives chi_H1=tr_C1-tr_C0+tr_H0. Signed fixed-facet enumeration, including half-turn and both even reflection types, produces each displayed rational dihedral trace. Independently rebuilt entire graphs and group actions for n=5..16 and verified all 252 dihedral elements; finite tests corroborate but do not prove the universal algebraic argument.

originality.rationale: The Lesh-Schreiner-Wahl original primary text defines the double D(X) and establishes weak Cohen-Macaulay connectivity bounds; Gale evenness classifies source facets. Neither statement calculates exact connected components or the rational D_n-character of D(boundary C(n,4)). Resultary searches for cyclic polytopes, dihedral homology and doubles returned other graph-complex actions (cycle matching, cut and polygonal multipath), not this double. Qualified priority: elementary graph proof could exist under an equivalent edge-partition/compatibility graph guise.

value.rationale: The boundary of a cyclic four-polytope is a canonical infinite family of simplicial 3-spheres, and doubling is a natural recently studied operator. The parity transition from a connected graph to exactly two components, together with a complete nontrivial dihedral H1 character, is a natural precise topological and equivariant classification for every n>=5.
